description: Small and separate: audit every surface that shows a game and confirm a LONG PRESS opens the detail sheet while a TAP launches. Add the long press where a surface lacks it. Tap-to-launch is not touched anywhere. Independent of FEAT-002 and FEAT-003 in code, but ordered last so the chooser it reaches is already there.
steps: Audit the four surfaces and record what each one has today. The planner's reading, to be re-checked against the code rather than trusted: CoverCard in native/ios/LibraryCards.swift (used by the Home shelves and by the All Games grid) has `.contentShape(Rectangle())`, `.onTapGesture { host.launch(entry:) }` and `.onLongPressGesture(minimumDuration: 0.4) { host.detailEntry = entry }` at around lines 270 to 276, so it is already correct. The List rows in native/ios/LibraryShell.swift at around lines 528 to 536 wrap GameListRow in the same pair, so they are correct. GameListRow itself in LibraryCards.swift carries an info Button that sets `host.detailEntry`, which stays. HeroCard in LibraryCards.swift has Play and More info pills and NO gesture on the art itself, so the hero is the gap.

Add to HeroCard, in native/ios/LibraryCards.swift, the same pair the cards use: `.contentShape(Rectangle())`, `.onTapGesture { host.launch(entry: entry) }` and `.onLongPressGesture(minimumDuration: 0.4) { host.detailEntry = entry }` on the hero's outer ZStack, with the same 0.4 second duration so the whole app has one long-press feel. The Play and More info pills and the favourite star are Buttons inside it and must keep working: a Button consumes its own tap, so the outer gestures must be attached where they do not shadow the pills. Verify by reading the view tree that the pills are inside the ZStack's `content` and that the scrim already has `.allowsHitTesting(false)`; if adding a tap gesture to the outer ZStack would swallow the pill taps, attach the gestures to the CoverArtView layer instead, which is the art the user presses, and say in a comment which one you chose and why.
Do NOT change tap-to-launch anywhere: no new confirmation, no changed target, no changed order of the two gestures on the surfaces that already have both.

Add a comment on HeroCard recording the rule in one sentence, matching the comment CoverCard already carries: a tap plays, a long press opens the detail sheet, and both are wired here so every surface in the app behaves the same way.
Write the audit result into the feature's findings field: each of the four surfaces, what it had before, and what it has now.
acceptance_criteria: Every surface that shows a game (hero, shelf card, grid card, list row) opens the detail sheet on a long press of about 0.4 seconds
Every one of those surfaces still launches the game on a tap, with no behaviour change to the tap
The hero's Play, More info and favourite controls still work as Buttons
The audit result for all four surfaces is recorded in the feature's findings field
swiftc -frontend -parse exits 0 for every .swift file under native/ios/ and cargo test still reports 74 passed
verification: cd native/ios && for f in *.swift; do swiftc -frontend -parse "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "ok $f" || echo "FAIL $f"; done
